sentence: Which sentence shows that you are not sure?
setupText: You cannot find your phone. You think it is in your bag, but you are not sure.
taskText: Which sentence shows that you are not sure?
text: You cannot find your phone. You think it is in your bag, but you are not sure. Which sentence shows that you are not sure?
options: My phone is in my bag.
My phone was in my bag.
Maybe my phone is in my bag.
My phone is not in my bag.
answer: Maybe my phone is in my bag.
explanation: 'Maybe' shows that the phone could be there, but you do not know.

This states the place as a fact; you have not found the phone yet.
'Maybe' shows that the phone could be there, but you do not know.
'Was' tells us about the past, not how sure you are now.
This says the bag is not the place; you have not checked it.

taskText: Complete the estimate: 'The trip takes ___ 30 minutes.'
text: The trip takes 28 or 32 minutes. The time changes a little. Complete the estimate: 'The trip takes ___ 30 minutes.'
answer: about
explanation: 'About 30' allows a little more or less than 30 minutes.

rationales.under: 'Under 30' means less than 30, but the trip can take 32.
rationales.about: 'About 30' allows a little more or less than 30 minutes.

sentence: Which answer gives that time exactly?

taskText: Which answer gives that time exactly?
text: Your appointment card says '10:00'. You want to give the exact time. Which answer gives that time exactly?
answer: It is at ten.
explanation: 'At ten' gives the time on the card without changing it into an estimate.

'At ten' gives the time on the card without changing it into an estimate.
'About ten' allows a time a little before or after ten.
'After ten' gives a later time than the card shows.
'Before ten' gives an earlier time than the card shows.

sentence: What does 'I think' show here?
setupText: Sara says, 'I think the blue coat is nicer.'
taskText: What does 'I think' show here?
text: Sara says, 'I think the blue coat is nicer.' What does 'I think' show here?
answer: Sara is giving her opinion.
explanation: 'I think' introduces Sara's own view about the coat.

Sara gives her view; she does not ask for an answer.
'I think' is present tense and does not give a past time.
She does not tell anyone to do something.
'I think' introduces Sara's own view about the coat.

sentence: Which reply says you do not know?
setupText: A coworker asks, 'Is Room 6 free?' You do not know.
taskText: Which reply says you do not know?
text: A coworker asks, 'Is Room 6 free?' You do not know. Which reply says you do not know?
answer: I'm not sure.
explanation: 'I'm not sure' tells the coworker that you do not know the answer.

This says you know the room is free.
'I'm not sure' tells the coworker that you do not know the answer.

sentence: Which sentence best describes how often you eat at home on workdays?
setupText: You work five days a week. You eat at home on four of those days.
taskText: Which sentence best describes how often you eat at home on workdays?
text: You work five days a week. You eat at home on four of those days. Which sentence best describes how often you eat at home on workdays?
answer: I usually eat at home.
explanation: 'Usually' fits something you do on most workdays, with an exception.

You eat at home on four days, so 'never' does not fit.
There is one workday when you do not eat at home.
'Usually' fits something you do on most workdays, with an exception.
'Rarely' means not often; four out of five days is often.

sentence: Which sentence correctly describes the red chairs?
setupText: There are ten chairs. Three are red and seven are blue.
taskText: Which sentence correctly describes the red chairs?
text: There are ten chairs. Three are red and seven are blue. Which sentence correctly describes the red chairs?
options: Some of the chairs are red.
Most of the chairs are red.
answer: Some of the chairs are red.
explanation: 'Some' fits the three red chairs without saying that all ten are red.

Seven chairs are blue, so they are not all red.
The description says three chairs are red.
Three out of ten is less than half, so 'most' does not fit.
'Some' fits the three red chairs without saying that all ten are red.

sentence: Which estimate is closest?

taskText: Which estimate is closest?
text: The price is $19.90. You want to give a simple estimate in whole dollars. Which estimate is closest?
answer: It costs about $20.
explanation: $19.90 is very close to $20, so this is a useful estimate.

$19.90 is very close to $20, so this is a useful estimate.
$10 is nearly ten dollars below the price.
$30 is more than ten dollars above the price.

sentence: Which sentence matches the cafe?
setupText: The cafe has twelve tables. Eleven are full and one is free.
taskText: Which sentence matches the cafe?
text: The cafe has twelve tables. Eleven are full and one is free. Which sentence matches the cafe?
options: Almost all the tables are full.
answer: Almost all the tables are full.
explanation: 'Almost all' fits eleven out of twelve, with just one exception.

Half of twelve is six; eleven tables are full.
'Almost all' fits eleven out of twelve, with just one exception.

sentence: How does Jo describe feeling?
setupText: After work, Jo says, 'I'm a little tired, but I can go for a walk.'
taskText: How does Jo describe feeling?
text: After work, Jo says, 'I'm a little tired, but I can go for a walk.' How does Jo describe feeling?
options: Jo is not tired at all.
Jo is tired, but not very tired.
Jo is too tired to walk.
answer: Jo is tired, but not very tired.
explanation: 'A little' limits the tiredness to a small degree.

'A little tired' means some tiredness, not none.
Jo says a walk is possible, so this adds a limit Jo does not give.
'Very' makes the tiredness stronger than 'a little'.
'A little' limits the tiredness to a small degree.

sentence: What does Tom mean?

taskText: What does Tom mean?
text: Tom says, 'Maybe I'll come to dinner.' What does Tom mean?
options: He has decided not to come.
He is not sure if he will come.
answer: He is not sure if he will come.
explanation: 'Maybe' leaves both coming and not coming possible.

'Maybe' means the decision is not certain.
He has not said no; coming is still possible.
'Maybe' leaves both coming and not coming possible.
'I'll come' is about the future, not yesterday.

sentence: Which sentence gives the exact number you counted?

options: There are more than eight cups.
There are fewer than eight cups.
answer: There are exactly eight cups.
explanation: 'Exactly' says that eight is the checked number, not an estimate.

'Exactly' says that eight is the checked number, not an estimate.

sentence: Which message gives this flexible time?

explanation: 'Around three' allows a few minutes before or after three.

'Around three' allows a few minutes before or after three.

sentence: Which sentence presents the destination as a guess?

answer: I think this bus goes to the airport.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-a1-1574:I think for an uncertain factual belief

'I think' presents the destination as your belief, with room for a mistake.

sentence: Which sentence matches the time?
setupText: A shop opens at nine and closes at six. You arrive at eight in the morning.
taskText: Which sentence matches the time?
text: A shop opens at nine and closes at six. You arrive at eight in the morning. Which sentence matches the time?
options: The shop is open until nine.
The shop is closed for the day.
The shop is not open yet.
answer: The shop is not open yet.
explanation: 'Not open yet' means it is closed now but will open later.

Eight is before opening time, so 'already open' does not fit.
Nine is the opening time, not the closing time.
'Not open yet' means it is closed now but will open later.
